name: FOAMULAR XPS
avoid_for: Bulk structural fill without full cement encapsulation
Exposed exterior — must be fully coated
supplier_notes: Available at COMEX, Home Depot MX, Bricolage
Check local foam suppliers — may carry under different brand names
price_observations: Approximately MXN 150–250 per sheet (2"x4'x8'), prices vary by thickness
risks: COMBUSTIBLE — must always be fully encapsulated in cement or non-combustible material
UV degradation if left uncoated
Toxic smoke when burned

name: EPS (Expanded Polystyrene)
common_sizes: Various — typically sold in blocks or custom-cut sheets
avoid_for: High-precision form work (less rigid than XPS)
supplier_notes: "Unicel" is the most common local brand in Mexico
Available at COMEX, hardware stores, sometimes block manufacturers
price_observations: Generally cheaper than XPS — MXN 80–150 per sheet depending on density
risks: COMBUSTIBLE — encapsulate fully
Lower compressive strength than XPS
Can absorb some moisture at edges if not sealed

name: AR Fiberglass Mesh
spanish_name: malla de fibra de vidrio resistente a álcalis
best_uses: Primary reinforcement layer in ferrocement shells
Crack resistance in thin-shell cement panels
Over foam forms before cement coat
avoid_for: Replacement with ordinary fiberglass cloth (degrades in cement)
supplier_notes: Harder to source locally in Puerto Vallarta — check tile/waterproofing suppliers
SIKA and other waterproofing suppliers sometimes carry AR mesh
price_observations: MXN 80–200 per sqm depending on weight and source
risks: Standard fiberglass cloth (boat fiberglass) is NOT a substitute for AR mesh in cement
Misidentification risk — always confirm alkali-resistant rating

name: Diamond Mesh
spanish_name: malla de alambre hexagonal / malla rombo
avoid_for: Wide-spanning structural elements without engineering review
supplier_notes: Widely available in Puerto Vallarta at ferreteras and construction suppliers
Galvanized preferred for exterior and wet conditions
price_observations: MXN 60–120 per roll — affordable and widely available
risks: Rust if not galvanized and cement encapsulation is poor
Opening too large for fine mortar mixes — match mesh to mix viscosity

name: Cattle Panel / Welded Wire
spanish_name: malla soldada / panel de alambre soldado
best_uses: Barrel roof primary structure — spans and curves
avoid_for: Thin shells (too heavy, too rigid for tight curves)
supplier_notes: Available at agricultural suppliers, some ferreteras
Often sold by agricultural/livestock supply stores in Mexico
price_observations: MXN 200–500 per panel depending on gauge and size
risks: Heavy — requires adequate support during forming
Rust risk if encapsulation is poor

name: Portland Cement
avoid_for: Exposure without waterproofing in coastal/humid environments without sealer
supplier_notes: Tolteca and Cruz Azul are the dominant brands in Jalisco
Available at any ferreterа or COMEX
risks: Caustic when wet — use gloves and eye protection
Requires damp curing for 7–28 days
Wrong water:cement ratio weakens the final material significantly

name: Fine Sand
common_sizes: Sold by cubic meter or in 50kg bags
supplier_notes: Aggregates suppliers throughout Puerto Vallarta — look for "materialeros"
Quality varies — sieve and wash if needed
risks: Clay contamination weakens mix — test quality before large batches
Salt contamination in coastal areas can cause reinforcement corrosion

name: SikaLatex
best_uses: Adhesion improver in cement/mortar coats over foam
avoid_for: Use as bulk structural binder — it is an admixture, not a primary binder
supplier_notes: Available at COMEX, Sika distributors in Puerto Vallarta
Follow manufacturer dilution ratio — typically 1:2 to 1:4 latex:water
price_observations: MXN 200–400 per liter — use sparingly per spec
risks: Overuse can trap moisture and cause delamination
Shelf life after opening — use within recommended period

name: Pegapiso / Porcelanato Adhesive
best_uses: Thin bond coat over foam or cementboard
avoid_for: Bulk structural use — NOT a structural material
Thick applications — it is a thin-coat adhesive
supplier_notes: Available at any tile/ferretería in Puerto Vallarta
Equivalent to US thinset in application method
risks: Often mistakenly used as a bulk structural material — INCORRECT use
Must be applied over properly primed/roughened substrate
